title: How the Marketplace Orders Replacement Charge Is Computed
content:
**Computation.** On Marketplace Orders, the replacement charge is the item price of the replaced units, that is the unit price times the units on the order's return requests whose reason allows a replacement (defective, damaged in transit, wrong item), plus the sales tax on that item price, which is the order's sales tax times that item price over the order's item subtotal plus shipping charge, each part rounded half up to the cent; an order with no replacement shipped owes no replacement charge.

## Parts of the charge

| Part | How it is worked out |
|---|---|
| Replaced units | the units recorded on the order's return requests whose reason is defective, damaged in transit or wrong item; none where no replacement has been shipped on the order |
| Item price | the unit price multiplied by the replaced units, rounded half up to the cent |
| Sales tax | the order's sales tax multiplied by the item price, divided by the order's item subtotal (unit price times units ordered) plus its shipping charge, rounded half up to the cent |
| Charge | the item price plus the sales tax, rounded half up to the cent, never below zero |

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A hypothetical order of 2 units at USD 45.00, shipping charge USD 0.00, sales tax USD 7.20, with a replacement shipped and one return request for 1 unit as defective:

1. Replaced units: 1.
2. Item price: 45.00 times 1, that is USD 45.00.
3. Sales tax: 7.20 times 45.00 divided by 90.00, that is USD 3.60.
4. Charge: 45.00 plus 3.60, that is USD 48.60.

An otherwise identical order on which no replacement was shipped owes no replacement charge.
